title: Before Dark Souls there was King's Field, and five hours into brilliant homage Queen's Domain, it's already one of my favourite games this year
description: The clue, of course, is right there in the title. Developer Freshly Baked Games' Queen's Domain isn't just a retro-fantasy action RPG played in first-person; it's an explicit homage to King's Field, the long-dormant FromSoftware series that - as the precursor to Demon's Souls, Dark Souls, Bloodborne, Sekiro, Elden Ring, and all those other Soulslikes - helped shape the modern gaming landscape in its own small way. That, though, is pretty much where my knowledge of the series begins and ends - as much as I love FromSoftware, I've never actually played a King's Field game. I've no idea how Queen's Domain shapes up as Kings Field-like, then, but I do know that, five or so hours in, it's already one of my favourite games this year. Read more

title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time’s 2026 Remake Looks Stunning Next To The Original N64 Game
description: Since its launch last year, the Switch 2 has proven itself to be a portable powerhouse, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake may just be the best game to show off its capabilities. The upgraded version of the timeless adventure looks even better when compared to the original N64 game that first debuted in 1998, as Nintendo has leveraged the Switch 2 hardware to create the definitive version of the game, blending atmospheric design with imaginatively designed character models. And if you want to see just how gorgeous that glow-up is, click the video below for a guided tour of Hyrule across two eras of Nintendo hardware. No commentary, just comparisons. For this video, we captured footage using an original NTSC 1.0 N64 cartridge running on an Analogue 3D with de-blur enabled. While there are a couple of Nintendo 64 emulators on the market, the Analogue 3D is generally considered to be the best of the lot. It's designed to capture the essence of a CRT TV display through various effects and filters. Ocarina of Time on the N64 was a game that had to work creatively around the limitations of the console and its cartridge system, at a time when the gaming industry was embracing CD-ROMs. Limitations do breed creativity, and the game is still fondly remembered for being a visual tour de force from an era when 3D games were making impressive strides. As for the Switch 2 version, the footage speaks for itself. It's crisp, the text is sharp, the extra effects are nice little touches, and the art direction has a Studio Ghibli feel to it. For more on the technical wizardry behind it, you can read our big The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake interview with producers Eiji Aonuma and Hidemaro Fujibayashi, as they spoke to GameSpot about what it took to modernize a classic game and keep its soul intact. "The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a reverent remake with stellar presentation, letting the original greatness shine through," Steve Watts wrote in GameSpot's…

title: This Handheld Gaming Hub Has A Lot More Going On Than You’d Expect
description: There's no shortage of dedicated video capture devices on the market, but if you're looking for something that cuts down on cable clutter and adds some cyberpunk vibes to your setup, you'll want to check out the Chizha Mount Ling 2 Pro. GameSpot recently went hands-on with it, and while it's a great capture device for PC handhelds like the Steam Deck and the Asus ROG Xbox Ally X, it's hard to recommend if you're planning to grab Switch 2 footage specifically. See on Kickstarter According to Chizha, the Mount Ling Pro 2can be used as a dock; it has a built-in capture card that can record gameplay at up to 4K 60fps, and you can install an NVMe solid-state drive (up to 4TB) in the bottom slot for your recording purposes. This essentially condenses multiple devices into one portable hub, and if that sounds good to you, you can check out the Kickstarter for it right now. If you pledge now, you can get the device for $150 for the version with a capture card, after which it will cost $250 at retail. One of the cool things about it is that it has a front display that will tell you what resolution your system is currently outputting as well as how much power you're drawing from it--useful information for content creators. In our testing, we found that it works very nicely with PC gaming handhelds, but there's still work to be done on the Switch 2 front. "I noticed that the color being displayed was a lot more washed out than when using an official Switch 2 dock," senior video producer Jean-Luc Seipke explained. "This happened when testing on our Samsung TV. When we tested it again using a portable monitor, however, everything looked consistent. I did speak this concern to the creators, and they told me it might be a firmware issue, and they're currently trying to sort out and fix it. The other issue I noticed is with upscaling. When running games that are clearly not 4K and are upscaled, I noticed that the quality of the image looked significantly worse than on the official…

title: Sony Is Getting Serious About The PS6, But Don’t Expect An Announcement Just Yet
description: With the PS5 entering its sixth year of active duty later this month, it looks like development on the yet-to-be-announced PS6 is picking up speed. During a briefing on its latest financial results, Sony said that research and development was proceeding smoothly on its "next-generation" platform. "Looking ahead to the next fiscal year, we aim to continue to enhance user engagement and further strengthen monetization through the release of strong titles and the expansion of our service. We also intend to make solid progress in preparing for the next-generation platform," Sony CFO Lin Tao said (via VGC ). Tao added that Sony will "attach great importance to a new platform and make the necessary investments for that," and an announcement will come "at an appropriate time in the future." Sony has kept tight-lipped on what users can expect from its next console, which will likely be an all-digital device as the company moves away from physical media in 2028. Price is another major factor, as earlier this year, Sony said that it was working out how to deal with the global component shortage crisis driven by various global factors. In May, Sony president and CEO Hiroki Totoki said that the rising costs for vital components like RAM would have an impact on its PS6 plans. "We have not yet decided on at what timing we will launch the new console, or at what prices," Totoki said. Analysts have predicted that the PS6 could sell for at least $1,000, which is looking likely. The PS5 Pro console saw its price hiked to $900 earlier this year, Valve's Steam Frame costs over $1,000, and one report says that the next-gen Xbox could cost as much as $1,800. With the ongoing memory shortage, Sony is expected to extend the lifecycle of the PS5, which is nearing lifetime sales of 100 million units.

title: PS5 Is Closing In On 100 Million Sales, Despite Getting More Expensive
description: During a briefing on its latest financial results, Sony revealed it sold 2.6 million PS5 consoles in its last quarter, which ended on September 30. This brings lifetime PS5 sales to 97.9 million, just months before the console enters its sixth year on the market. By comparison, the PS4 had shipped 103.0 million units at the same point in its lifecycle, but Sony's gaming ecosystem is performing much better thanks to higher digital revenue and a massive active user base. This comes at a time when the PS5 has only gotten more expensive since launch, thanks to the global components shortage that has seen memory prices surge. Sony says it has been in discussions with manufacturers to secure enough memory for the next fiscal year and expects its hardware sales to remain profitable into the next year. The company has raised its forecast, as it expects sales of first- and third-party games--like GTA 6--to increase. GTA 6 is projected to have sold almost 8 million copies ahead of its November 19 launch, and PS5 sales are said to be dominating by a wide margin compared with Xbox Series X|S. Sony also keeps 30% of the revenue from the game through platform fees, so GTA 6's early success will only improve PlayStation's fortunes. With manufacturing adjustments that make the PS5 cheaper to produce and monetization of its monthly active users--which peaked at 127 million in September--business looks solid for Sony's game division. Sony also touched on plans for its next PlayStation console, saying it's making "solid progress" on development and will announce it at an "appropriate time" in the future.

title: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time’s NPCs Stay Busy All Night, And Sounds Like That Was A Pain
description: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2 is a mostly faithful remake, but it does introduce some new features and bells and whistles that modernize the experience. Some of those are very noticeable, like the addition of a jump button, while others are more subtle. One such subtle change is the new full-day passage of time inside Hyrule Castle Town, which also means NPCs need something to do all night. And according to producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi, that meant a ton of extra work, especially for him. "I reviewed every single text of the NPCs," Fujibayashi told GameSpot. "And before, in the original game, each NPC didn't have a strict 24-hour routine, but in this game, they do. The director said, 'We want to have a 24-hour routine for every NPC.' And in my mind, I was like, 'That's going to be a lot of work.' [laughs] And I told them, 'That's going to be a lot of work,' but they said they want to do it. So in my heart, I was like, 'Okay, I guess I'm committed.' "Because on the one hand, I know it's going to be a lot of work, but I also didn't want to discourage the young staff from coming up with new ideas and taking on new challenges," he continued. "So I had to roll up my sleeves and, on a daily basis, try to check as much of the dialogue as possible, working with the team, discussing what can be tweaked, what can be adjusted. So all of that to say that it was a lot of work." The idea of a younger generation coming up with new ideas to modernize Ocarina of Time was a repeated theme during our wide-ranging interview with producers Eiji Aonuma and Hidemaro Fujibayashi, as well as how the more experienced developers would push the younger class to rethink their assumptions. Ocarina of Time is enjoying stellar reviews across the board, including in GameSpot's 9/10 review. Currently it is also the top-rated game of 2026 on GameSpot sister site Metacritic.

title: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Accidentally Made ReDeads Too Scary At One Point
description: Every The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time player remembers their first encounter with the ReDeads. The shambling zombie-like enemies occupy Hyrule Castle Town when you emerge from the Temple of Time and immediately freak you out, with a sudden piercing scream that freezes you in place. The new ReDeads work largely the same way, but at one point in development they were made significantly scarier. "With this remake, the graphics are a lot improved, and so the ReDead--the sound, the graphics, and the movement--ended up being very, very scary," producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi told GameSpot via a translator. "And the staff wanted to make this in service of making a good gameplay experience. But from our perspective, taking a step back, we felt like, let's remember the experience that we don't want to change, and taking that into consideration, maybe we've gone a step too far, so let's dial it back." As Fujibayashi and fellow producer Eiji Aonuma mentioned several times in our wide-ranging interview, this project was full of younger staffers who had new ideas for how to modernize the classic, while also learning the ropes of a classic Zelda design. Those young guns may have had a different idea of what constitutes a scary moment in a Zelda game, especially if the already-spooky ReDead were made too spooky. The ReDead have been slightly revised from their original version, with clearer visual indicators to show their gaze and a red vine-like tendril to signify your frozen state. They can still be pretty alarming, but once you understand how to beat them the new indicators make it easier to avoid their attack and strike them from behind. Those careful details are part of why I called this version of Ocarina of Time the "definitive way to experience this all-time classic" in my Zelda: Ocarina of Time review, and why it's currently the top-rated game of 2026 on GameSpot sister site Metacritic.

title: Nintendo Explains How It Made The Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Only It Could Create
description: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is one of Nintendo's most revered games of all time, even by the lofty standards of a company known for making influential, groundbreaking video games. That legacy means extra care and consideration put into remaking the game for modern audiences on the Nintendo Switch 2, with a remake that is receiving a glowing reception both in our GameSpot review and across the industry. It is now the top-ranked game of 2026 on GameSpot sister site Metacritic. It's a titanic achievement, but to hear producers Eiji Aonuma and Hidemaro Fujibayashi, it was also intended as a learning experience for both the new generation, and for themselves. In a wide-ranging interview just hours ahead of the release of the game, the two repeatedly came back to how younger staff, some of whom had never played the original game, were both discovering the craft of classic Zelda design and introducing their own bold new ideas. They talked about what needed to be modernized, and what was important to preserve, in creating what I called "definitive way to experience this all-time classic." The interview below was conducted via interpreters. It has been edited for length and clarity. GameSpot: In your Ask the Developer QA you said you remember the feeling of nervousness and anticipation leading up to the original launch of Ocarina. So I have to ask: How are you feeling today? Eiji Aonuma: How am I feeling today? Well, since we've arrived in New York, we've had these really good opportunities to talk to media. These are folks who, of course, got early copies of the game for the purpose of reviews. And I got to hear about their experiences playing, and some of them talked about being moved to tears while playing, which was amazing for me to hear. And now knowing that with the official release, many more people will be able to play and share their experiences with us. So, yes, I would say that my nerves have calmed quite a bit, and I'm feeling very happy right now.…

title: How Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Benefits From A Glaringly Obvious Tactic That Few Game Devs Follow
description: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has been regarded as one of the best games ever made for nearly 30 years, and its new Switch 2 remake is seeing similar levels of acclaim. Part of the reason for its critical success seems to be its deep understanding of the source material, and that shouldn't be a surprise when considering how well Nintendo has retained staff over the years--something very few other game companies have managed to do. Speaking to GameSpot, longtime Zelda producer Eiji Aonuma acknowledged the benefits of having developers on the team who have been working at Nintendo for decades. "I think you see a real benefit to having some very long-term-tenured staff members around who have shared the same experiences over time, because every time you get to the next step, it's easier to discuss how to proceed, or if you're going to do something new," Aonuma said via an interpreter. "When you have new staff coming in, of course you want to make sure that you're bringing everyone up with a lot of discussion, explaining how to do things, why you're doing things certain ways, as well as the language that you're using. But that takes some more time, as well. So you need a bit of a balance." Despite not having everyone move from one Zelda project to the next, enough developers have remained at Nintendo to provide a consistent throughline. "And so you do see the Zelda team change over time, but there is a continuity of core staff--certainly at least from one project to the next--so that we have that base that we can build from and bring up new staff with it," Aonuma added. "And this is something that I think Nintendo has done for a very long time, even since Miyamoto [was] originally working on projects like this. And it contributes to some of the sense of continuity that you do feel in games in the Zelda franchise, for example." "Continuity" might not be the first thing you think of when Zelda gets mentioned, but Nintendo certainly knows what it's doing with Zelda…

title: Nintendo Wanted Ocarina Of Time To Feel Better In The Remake, Not Just Different
description: Remaking a game like The Legend of Zelda: The Ocarina of Time required Nintendo to nail a fine balance between staying faithful to the original and updating it where it mattered. The Ocarina of Time remake largely sticks to the original's foundations while adding features like a dedicated jump button and updated controls. That was one of several changes, as Nintendo's core design philosophy was to modernize execution and comfort while preserving the original emotional and narrative intent. As Legend of Zelda producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi explained in an interview with GameSpot, early pre-production focused on setting clear boundaries for what would and wouldn't change in the remake. "One of the first discussions we had leading up to the full-blown development of the title was really clearly establishing what it is we were going to change and what it is that we weren't going to change," Fujibayashi said via a translator. "Starting with the kind of stuff that we wanted to change, was really focused on leveraging the capabilities of the Nintendo Switch 2 hardware because it was going to be developed for that hardware. Leveraging all that capability so that we can remove any stress from the gameplay experience so that people can enjoy the game, fully." In addition to the changes in the game's controls, Fujibayashi added that the updated graphics also allowed the team to "provide a lot more information" to players, and the sound design also got a big upgrade: 5.1-channel surround sound for the background music. To reduce friction, the team concluded that a dedicated jump action would give players more agency to explore the world without changing the core experience. "There was a lot of heavy discussion, as you mentioned, about the jump button," Fujibayashi said. "Ultimately, we ended up in the conclusion that being able to allow players to jump anywhere will make the gameplay experience a lot smoother and allow players to be really able to fully enjoy the experience…

title: WoW: Forever’s Launch Is Going Surprisingly Smooth
description: World of Warcraft: Forever's launch hit some minor hiccups immediately upon release, but overall is going surprisingly well, much to the surprise of players who anticipated the worst. As soon as the countdown timer clicked to zero at 3 PM PT, players began to encounter short login queues. Sitting through the queue would bring up the game's list of possible rulesets, but they were grayed out an unavailable. It took around 30 minutes of players requeuing and waiting with bated breath to see if the servers would come online or if they were out of luck, but lo and behold, eventually everything started working as intended. In all previous versions of WoW, players picked a server to call home and create their character on, then logged in to that server to play. Servers generally ranged from anywhere between 3,000 to 10,000 or more players, with server sizes increasing in recent years as Blizzard experimented with larger, but fewer, servers. In the past, that approach to WoW Classic launches have seen their fair share of issues, from hours-long queues to login issues. For Forever, Blizzard opted for a different, "realmless" approach. Instead of individual servers, players would instead pick their desired "ruleset," like player vs. environment, roleplaying, or player vs. player. All players on the same ruleset are then placed on essentially one giant mass of interconnected servers. So far, that seems to have been a good call. Aside from the first 30 minutes, launch has been smooth, with minimal lag and few issues. Starting zones are crowded, but it's not impossible to make progress on quests. Some players on Reddit are calling it "possibly the best Blizzard launch ever," with another saying they've "never seen a smoother launch." In other Forever news, Blizzard gave all classes a big damage boost ahead of launch, is teasing what looks to be a new legendary weapon players will be able to acquire, and even hinted at new class and race combos that could be coming to the game…

title: WoW: Forever May Have Just Sneakily Revealed New Class And Race Combos
description: Developer Blizzard may have just revealed new World of Warcraft: Forever class and race combos less than a day before the game's launch. Forever already features a number of new class and race combos not seen in WoW Classic, like troll Warlocks, human Hunters, and more. In a launch overview video diving into what players need to know about this new version of Blizzard's genre-defining MMORPG, however, eagle-eyed players noticed a few peculiar sights. Along what appeared to be various class abilities that aren't currently in the game, certain class and race combinations that aren't currently possible can also be seen. A total of three new race and class combos are shown in the footage, including a tauren Mage casting frostbolt, a skyborne Paladin, and what appears to be a night elf Shaman (or at least a night elf wearing a Shaman armor set). Those would each be big additions, particularly when it comes to more options for Paladin and Shaman players. Currently in Forever, only dwarves can be Shamans on the Alliance side of the MMO's faction divide, while the only Paladin option on Horde is undead. Having additional choices is never a bad thing, and a second Shaman option would likely be well received by the game's community. Since skyborne can be either faction, this would give Horde players another race choice for Paladin, but could also ruffle some feathers. Skyborne are currently locked behind a $30 paywall, and some players might not take kindly to having a new paladin option cost additional cash. Though it's certainly possible the new race and class combos seen in the launch overview video were included by mistake and no longer something Blizzard is planning, that seems unlikely given Blizzard's past comments. While they won't be included in the game at launch, Blizzard has made clear they are something players should be expecting in the near future. title: GTA 6 Will Now Come To Stores Sooner, But It’s Not Playable Right Away
description: Rockstar Games has announced that Grand Theft Auto 6 will now released in stores two days earlier than anticipated--but this doesn't change anything about when you'll actually be able to play the game. GTA 6's code-in-a-box physical edition will be available to purchase in stores starting on November 10; it was previously going to be November 12. Rockstar also moved up the preloading date for GTA 6 from November 12 to November 10 for the digital and code-in-a-box versions. The developer offered no explanation as to why it made these changes, and the company did not respond to GameSpot's request seeking comment. While you might walk into a Target or Best Buy or GameStop on November 10 and see a copy of GTA 6 that you can spend real money on, you cannot actually play the game until November 19 when the game goes live. If you're in the US, you'll be among the last people in the world to get in due to how the game is launching non-simultaneously. Also in the post, Rockstar confirmed what everyone expected: The $100 Ultimate Edition of GTA 6 is not going to be sold in stores. This move, along with ditching discs entirely, is all about making money. GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. A recent poll said lots of people are excited to play GTA Online, but GTA 6 is a single-player game with no multiplayer component, at least not yet.
